question: A network engineer must configure a power redundancy policy on a Cisco UCS C-Series Rack Server. The power redundancy must support two power sources being used to power the server. Which configuration should be applied to meet the requirement?
options:
server# scope org /
server /org # scope psu-policy
server /org/psu-policy # set redundancy N+1
server /org/psu-policy* # commit-buffer

server# scope org /
server /org # scope psu-policy
server /org/psu-policy # set redundancy grid
server /org/psu-policy* # commit-buffer

server# scope org /
server /org # scope psu-policy
server /org/psu-policy # set psu-redundancy-policy N+1
server /org/psu-redundancy-policy* # commit-buffer

server# scope org /
server /org # scope psu-policy
server /org/psu-policy # set psu-redundancy-policy grid
server /org/psu-redundancy-policy* # commit-buffer
theory: Cisco UCS C-Series power supply redundancy policies include options like grid, N+1, and non-redundant; 'grid' redundancy specifically means the server's power supplies are split across two independent power sources/grids, so a failure of one entire input feed (not just one PSU) still leaves the server powered. N+1 protects against a single PSU failure but assumes a common power source, so it does not satisfy a requirement to tolerate loss of one of two separate power feeds — only the grid redundancy setting does. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS C-Series Power Management)
